day: Our Lady of Sorrows on Tuesday of week 24 in Ordinary Time
text:
There is a loneliness in loss that can make us feel unmoored, untethered. When everything we thought solid seems to be taken from us, we may wonder: who gathers us in? The cross of Jesus is a place of profound sorrow, and yet from that place of deepest darkness, Jesus does something tender. He does not leave his mother alone. He places her into a beloved son's care. He places the beloved disciple into her care. Out of death itself, he weaves new bonds.

The first reading reminds us that we are not solitary pilgrims. We are a body made of many different parts, each necessary, each called to offer something different. Yet being part of this body means that when one of us stumbles, we are held. When one of us grieves, we are received. The shepherd knows his sheep, the psalm tells us. None of us is ever truly cast loose.

Today, on this feast day honoring Mary's sorrows, we might sit quietly with the image of Jesus making sure his mother would not grieve alone. It is a small gesture amid immeasurable pain, yet in it lies something deeply true: we are meant to hold one another. We are meant to make room for each other in our homes, in our hearts.

Is there someone whose sorrow you might sit with today, not to fix it, but simply to say: I am here?
